iut_type: Registration deadline tied to public disclosure date -- encompasses press releases, preview events, website announcements, and dealer pamphlet distribution, not just the actual sale date
customer_question: We're planning to launch our branded product on April 1 -- by when must we complete registration and the SIG wire transfer relative to that date?
question_variants: If we hold a preview event or send marketing pamphlets to retailers before our official sale date, does that change our registration deadline?
Does the registration deadline track the actual product sale date, or something earlier?
actual_issue: The customer assumed their registration deadline was tied to their planned brand sales launch date (April 1) and asked for guidance on exactly when registration and the corresponding Qualification Fee wire transfer needed to be completed relative to that date.
plain_english_explanation: SIG's actual requirement is to complete registration by the date a third party becomes aware of the existence of your Bluetooth-equipped product -- this is not necessarily the same as the official sale date. If any of the following occur before the planned sale date, the registration (and its public listing) must be completed by that earlier date instead: a press release, a preview/open-house event, an announcement on a website, or even sending marketing pamphlets to retail dealers. In other words, the actual sale date is just one of several possible disclosure triggers -- any public-facing or even retailer-facing announcement activity that reveals the product's existence ahead of the sale date moves the effective registration deadline earlier. Separately, the Qualification Fee wire transfer to SIG must be completed by your own bank the day before you perform the actual registration finalization operation, since registration cannot be finalized until SIG has received the payment.
consultant_answer: SIG's requirement is to register by whichever date a third party first becomes aware that your Bluetooth-equipped product exists -- this isn't necessarily your sale date. If you have a press release, preview event, website announcement, or even send pamphlets to dealers before your planned sale date, you'd need to register and have the listing public by that earlier date instead. Also, make sure the Qualification Fee wire transfer reaches SIG the day before you actually finalize the registration, since SIG won't let registration complete until payment is received.
decision_logic: When a customer states a target registration date based on their planned sale date, ask whether any earlier public-facing or dealer-facing disclosure activities (press releases, preview events, website announcements, dealer pamphlet distribution) are planned, since SIG's actual deadline is tied to the earliest such disclosure event rather than the sale date itself.
final_recommendation: When scoping a registration timeline against a customer's stated sale date, proactively ask about any planned pre-launch disclosure activities (marketing, events, dealer materials) that could move the effective registration deadline earlier than the sale date itself.
risk_if_done_wrong: A customer who plans registration around their sale date without accounting for earlier disclosure events (press releases, dealer pamphlets, preview events) could end up disclosing the product's existence before completing registration, violating SIG's certification timing requirement.
